business: HomeWalk (hellohomewalk.com): turns a builder's 2D house plans into a browser-based 3D walkthrough and photoreal stills before the home is built
by_segment: Owner of a small custom builder (1-6 homes a year, client brings or hires an architect)
Sales, marketing or drafting lead at a spec/production builder with a library of 20-100+ plans
Owner of a mid-size custom/semi-custom builder (7-20 homes a year)
by_behaviour: Lost their renderer / open to a vendor
Architect or in-house team already covers it
Sells with photos of finished homes
why_not: We already get renders and plans through the architect or our in-house people, and I'm in my truck between lots most days. I'm not adding a vendor and a per-home fee when the homeowner would have to agree to pay it anyway.

My architect already does 3D for us, and I bill architecture and pre-construction cost-plus, so a new $1,500 line only goes in if the homeowner agrees to pay it. I'm not going to eat that cost or add a vendor to a process that already works.

I do 1-6 homes a year and my clients come from referrals. They hire an architect and the architect already shows them the plans. Nobody has ever asked me for a walkthrough before we break ground, so I'd be paying $1,500 a home to solve a problem my buyers don't tell me they have.

Our architect and in-house drafter already turn out renders and models as part of the plan package, so I'd be paying twice for something I already get. I'm not putting $1,500 a house on a library of 20-100 plans.

I do 1-6 homes a year and most of my work comes from referrals, so a walkthrough isn't something I'm missing right now. I don't have the capacity to think about this, and the boss decides on website stuff anyway.
I'm in the truck between job sites all day and I don't have the capacity to think about this right now. If it showed up in my inbox I'd say 'email me something' and never get back to it.

I bill cost-plus, so I wouldn't eat $1,500 a home across a big plan library, and I'd only add it as a line item if the homeowner agrees to pay. Most of my buyers are spec and Parade of Homes traffic who walk a model or look at renderings I already have.
I bill cost-plus, so I'm not eating $1,500 a home out of my own pocket. I'd only add it as a line if the homeowner agrees, and the architect already gives my clients renderings.

I build 1-6 custom homes a year and half of them change after the architect hands me plans. I'm not putting something on my website that might show a client a house we won't build. Also the boss decides, and I'm on a job site, not looking at this.

My buyers pick from a standard plan library and the cost-plus pass-through means I'd only add a line item if the homeowner agrees to pay, and most won't for a renderings line. I'd also worry it shows finishes or options we won't actually build and sets us up for a dispute.
why_yes: My renderer is gone and I need someone reliable. A free first plan with no deposit and pay-only-if-I-like-it means I lose nothing by trying, and $1,500 a home is small next to what a change order costs once framing starts.
My renderer is gone and I need someone reliable, and the free test on one of my own plans with no deposit makes it easy to try. $1,500 a home is fine since I bill it through the pre-con line anyway.

My renderer is gone and I do need someone, and a free build of one of my plans with no deposit costs me nothing but a lunch. I'd pay for one plan if it looks right, but I'm not committing to a batch until I see it.

Clients keep asking me to show them the house before we build, and no deposit with pay-only-if-I-like-it means I risk a lunch. If it looks right and I can pass the $1,500 through on the architecture line, I'd run it on one plan.
